findings.what: The E10 watch horizon contradicts the pre-registration. The main session told the user (08:2xZ, plan table) that it watches for an x138 successor only until 27 Sep 12:00 UTC and that the slots then stay empty. The pre-registered E10/C10 says to poll every 4-6 h until 29 Sep 07:00 UTC. The §e slot table has S8 (27 Sep) and S14 (28 Sep, 'наследник x138 по позднему триггеру'), and KNOWLEDGE W23 also runs to 29 Sep 07:00. A successor port is a verbatim public notebook, not a new mechanism of ours, so the R8 27 Sep 12:00 cutoff does not end E10. R8's other clause ('после 29.09 02:00 только аварийный повтор') does cap it: the last successor submit is 29 Sep 02:00, and with ~1.5 h for pull, dummy and OK, the last useful trigger is ~29 Sep 00:00 UTC. The pre-reg's '29 Sep 07:00' is therefore internally inconsistent with R8 and should be read as 29 Sep 00:00. Ending the watch at 27 Sep 12:00 drops ~36 h of the E10 window (roughly half of the remaining P(trigger)).

findings.what: No pre-registered admission rule or finals pair exists for an E10 port, and the rules as written block it. (a) §f(iii) says F1 must contain C01. E10 says 'port verbatim', and C10's 'add C01's --set if it keeps x138's guard' is not buildable: tools/build_probe_kernel.py has only the exp39 and x138 bases, and --patch safetail exits unless --base x138. Adding a successor base is new code after R8 and breaks 'verbatim'. As written, a successor at 0.956 could only be a §f 'simpler file' at +0.002, and even that needs (iii). (b) The READ TABLE/v2-v4 pairs cover only K2, twin, K1, K2'', #34 and exp52, so the pair after a port scores (port + K2? port + twin?) is undefined, and choosing it after seeing the score would be post-hoc. (c) runtime_ledger.py maps only the exp56/exp57*/exp58* tokens. A port gets family 'unknown', which prints R5(a) 'n/a'. Its R5(a) deadline depends on whether it keeps x138's REPAIR_DEADLINE_S = 27000 guard (7.5 h). (d) The C10 hygiene conditions are not in CONTEXT: all sources public, a diff vs exp56 of 1-2 explainable mechanisms, no in-kernel PP sweep or validator on test stems, no cached-CSV or test-derived dataset (koushikrudra consensus type), and no public knob ladder (C10: 'private ~0 or negative for a public-swept knob set'). Every E10 port also needs the user's OK. The user sleeps at night (UTC+3), so a trigger at ~20:00-04:00Z could lose up to 8 h or miss S14.

findings.what: The Kaggle API/CLI cannot read either quantity the endgame depends on. (1) ApiSubmission has no 'selected' field (fields: date, description, error_description, file_name, private_score, public_score, ref, status, submitted_by, team_name, total_bytes, url), so neither the poller nor any script can confirm that #37 and #38 are ticked. The '29.09 12:00 проверю, что отмечены' promise needs the Submissions web page (Claude in Chrome, read-only) or a user screenshot. (2) The kernel-list API has no score field (fields: ref, title, last_run_time, total_votes, ...). `--sort-by scoreDescending` orders by score but does not print it, so a CLI E10 check can only detect a CHANGE: a new ref entering the top of the score-sorted list (at 08:30Z the top 4 were raunakdey07/biohub-harmonic-fusion-v3, amanatar/optimized-biohub-max-score, kunaldesale2408/biohub-cell-tracking and anvithpothula/biohub-0-953-lb-original, all 0.953 per the round-5/6 browser scans), or a new dateRun entry. The score must then be read in the browser. Separately, no CONTEXT entry confirms that the user actually ticked #37 + #38. The 07:35Z entry says 'tick now', and WATCHLIST W54 is 'not started'.
